wa_east_face_5.blurb: East Face is the side of Big Rock that looks east over the Rocks of Sharon outcrops near Spokane. It holds about fifteen climbs, mostly bolted sport lines with a handful of trad cracks, so a rack is only needed for part of it. The grades start at easy fifth class and reach the low 5.11s, with the bulk sitting in the 5.7 to 5.10 range, which suits a mixed party of newer and experienced leaders. The face is on the quieter side, and some of the cracks are still dirty. Expect a short uphill hike to reach it.
wa_east_face_5.approach: From the trail that climbs from the Stevens Creek Road parking area, walk up to the toe where the south and east faces meet. The east face starts there and rises along the trail to the right.

wa_elephant_ridge.blurb: Elephant Ridge is a basalt ridge at Cape Disappointment on the Long Beach Peninsula, close to the Pacific. Its ocean-facing west side carries mainly bolted sport lines, plus a few top-rope variations, a small number of trad pitches and some short boulder problems. Most of the roped climbs fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with the 5.10s and 5.11s making up the core, and the problems are easy to moderate. The rock is textured and generally solid, though coastal moss and a loose, exposed fourth-class crest above the faces are worth keeping in mind. The ridge is also a way into the neighbouring Amphitheater.

wa_goliath_boulder_the.blurb: The Goliath Boulder is a wooded bouldering spot on Mt Erie above Anacortes, on Fidalgo Island. It is a single large boulder with fifteen problems that cover an unusually wide range, from easy V0 warm-ups through the middle grades to a few lines up to V9 for strong boulderers. One visitor calls it among the best boulders in the region. Reaching it means a walk uphill from the base of Mt Erie, then a clearing beyond the power lines, so it is best for a focused session rather than a roadside stop.

wa_jerry_garcia_boulder.blurb: The Jerry Garcia boulder is the first boulder you meet at The Egg, a small roadside bouldering zone along Icicle Creek near Leavenworth. It is the largest cluster there, with about fifteen problems, and its chalked holds can be spotted from where you park. Most are easy to moderate, from V0 and below up to around V4, which makes it friendly for beginners and a decent warm-up, while a few harder lines run from V6 up to V8. Several of the problems are well-liked classics, and Musashi, a standout nearby, sits on the next boulder over.

wa_machine_gun_boulder.blurb: Machine Gun Boulder is a single secluded block high in Icicle Canyon, near Leavenworth. There are around fifteen problems, with room for traverses and eliminates, and nearly all of them are easy: mostly V1 and V2 with a few V3s and one V0. That makes it a relaxed place for a short warm-up session or a couple of quiet hours rather than a hard-project destination. The boulder sits back from the road a short way and is reportedly tough to spot from the pavement, so having a passenger watch for the pullout helps.

wa_midnight_rock.blurb: Midnight Rock is a steep trad crag above Tumwater Canyon near Leavenworth, noted as one of the best crack crags in Washington. All fifteen climbs are trad and demanding: about half are 5.10, and the rest are 5.11 and 5.12. The style mixes face climbing, finger cracks and a lot of wide cracks, so you need a full rack and solid crack technique. It is not a beginner or casual place. Expect a long, steep uphill hike before you start, so plan for a committed day.

wa_mordor.blurb: Mordor is the far east end of the main cliff band at Ozone, in the Columbia Gorge on the Washington side. It is steeper than the rest of the crag and has several roofs, and it is the place at Ozone for harder, pumpy sport climbing. Of its fifteen routes, most are bolted. The grades run from 5.8 up through the 5.10s, with the 5.11s and 5.12s making up most of the lines. The walk from the road is short, along the base of the cliff to the east end, about five minutes.
